title: Kill Blue
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Juzo Ogami, a 39-year-old star hitman for the Z.O.O. syndicate, is stung by a genetically altered wasp and regresses to age 13. Sent to a middle school to vet it for his boss's daughter, the never-schooled Ogami finds he loves school life while juggling assassin rivals and Noren Mitsuoka, heiress of the pharmaceutical company that may hold his cure.
life_message: It is never too late to experience the friendship and growth that an ordinary youth offers.

content.note: Hitman protagonist with guns and rival assassin groups (Wikipedia); AniList and MangaUpdates tag assassins and guns. An Otaku USA writer likens it to Case Closed with more violence.
Assassin fights and organized crime; comedic school tone balances.
A reviewer notes worrying potential for romance between adult-minded Ogami and Noren but says it is handled well (Wikipedia); a classmate has a crush on him.
Not reported; shonen action norms (to verify).
A classmate with a split personality (Wikipedia; AniList Dissociative Identities tag), presented comically.
Professional killer shown as cool and capable.

dominant: Second chance at youth; friendship and school community; professional competence

frames.aligns: Ogami discovers friendship, learning and the goodness of ordinary youth.
frames.concerns: A hired killer as hero without clear repentance.

frames.aligns: Renewal and humility in a hardened man.
Joy in learning and vocation as student.
Valuing simple school life over violence.

frames.concerns: Killing for hire; adult-minded hero with schoolgirls.
Gun glamor; reviewer flags age-gap romance risk.

frames.aligns: Competence, loyalty and appreciation of schooling.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Rival assassins and the 'Demon's Left Hand' reputation drive confrontations (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: School rules and syndicate orders, with comic rule-bending.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to syndicate and to new classmates.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Elite 'Unicorn' students and assassin ranks exist; friendships cut across them.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Ogami trades survival work for enjoying club life.

folkways.japan: Middle-school club culture, senpai-kohai relations and the idea of youth (seishun) as a precious stage shape the comedy.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers praise characters and premise, none mention lecturing (Wikipedia reception).
delivery.note: The value of schooling comes through Ogami's enjoyment rather than speeches.

winners_losers: Ogami gains the youth he never had; rival assassins lose fights; school friendship gets the sympathy.
to_verify: Graphic level of gun violence in the manga.
How the Ogami and Noren relationship resolves by the final volume.
